ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all beneficial owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories, controlling persons, and relevant counterparties before incorporation and periodically thereafter against United Nations Security Council lists, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, United Nations Act, and related regulations, applicable OFAC lists where a United States nexus exists, and Canadian politically exposed person and head-of-international-organization requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Resolve false positives using date of birth, nationality, address, and documentary evidence. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, sanctioned-country exposure, opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, adverse media, unexplained wealth, and high-risk payment activity. File suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC where legally required; do not disclose the filing or its existence to the subject.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent; Alberta does not generally provide direct public self-service incorporation filing for all corporate transactions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporation may use an English, French, or combined English-French name. The name must comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and regulations, be distinctive, not be confusing with an existing corporate or business name, and not imply an unauthorized governmental, professional, financial, or regulated activity. A translated or transliterated version does not automatically create separate name protection. Trade names and corporate names are distinct registrations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a regulated profession or public authority
Words requiring consent or approval under applicable Alberta or federal legislation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain an Alberta NUANS or equivalent name-search report through an authorized registry agent, confirm corporate-name eligibility, and submit the proposed name with the incorporation application. If rejected, obtain the written reason, correct the distinguishing element or remove a sensitive term, and resubmit through the registry agent. Where the decision is based on an alleged conflict, provide evidence of distinctiveness, consent, prior authorization, or existing rights. Seek review or administrative reconsideration from Alberta Corporate Registry where available; a statutory judicial review application may be considered in the Alberta Court of King's Bench after available administrative remedies are exhausted. Name reservation periods and report expiry must be verified with the registry agent because they may differ by filing type and document.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Alberta corporation must maintain a registered office in Alberta and an address for service that satisfies the Alberta Business Corporations Act and registry requirements. A commercial registered-office or virtual-office provider may be acceptable for statutory service if it maintains the required records, receives and promptly forwards service, and provides a genuine Alberta address. A mailbox-only, accommodation, or non-operational address is unsuitable. For FPV racing-drone retail, carbon-fiber milling, brushless-motor integration, inventory, product testing, importation, or customer returns, a virtual office does not establish sufficient operational substance and may be rejected by banks, payment processors, insurers, customs authorities, or tax authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No statutory probability is published. For a low-regulatory-risk Alberta drone retailer with transparent ownership, an estimated unannounced physical-inspection risk is approximately 5–15% in the first operating year, subject to material increases for customs issues, complaints, product-safety concerns, unusual payment activity, tax inconsistencies, sanctions exposure, or an implausible registered address. Canadian tax, customs, corporate-registry, workplace-safety, and product-safety authorities may conduct risk-based inquiries or inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended, ss. 12, 15, 101, 102, 210 and 212 (unlimited liability corporation provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation with issuance of Certificate of Incorporation by the Alberta Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); the directors may fix the consideration for share subscription. No escrow account or capital deposit is required unless the terms of the share subscription agreement expressly impose one. For a ULC, the unlimited liability clause must appear in the Articles and be reflected in the share certificate wording.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopt the Articles of Incorporation as filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial share subscription be accepted, common shares be issued for consideration fixed by the board, and share certificates be delivered upon full payment. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [Registered Office Address, Alberta] and that [Registered Agent] be appointed to receive process on behalf of the Corporation. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [President], [Secretary] and [Treasurer] be appointed officers with authority to open banking accounts, execute banking documents, purchase directors and officers insurance, and file all statutory returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct NUANS Name Search and Reserve Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through Service Alberta authorized service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request to the Alberta Corporate Registry system, specifying the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Reserve a name that is distinctive from all existing Alberta corporate names and permissible under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). The reservation is valid for 90 days and must be filed with the Articles of Incorporation before expiry.
required_dossiers: Government-issued photo identification of incorporator or authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for confusion with an existing corporate name, file a revised name reservation with a written consent from the conflicting name holder or choose a new distinct corporate name; no refund of name search fees is provided.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Incorporation and Supporting Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the prescribed Articles of Incorporation for an unlimited liability corporation, including the corporate name, full registered office address in Alberta, number of directors, authorized share structure, restrictions on business, and the unlimited liability clause. Complete the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, and obtain signed consents from each first director.
required_dossiers: Consent of each director to act as first director
Statement of unlimited shareholder liability for ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a requisition for incomplete particulars, correct and resubmit the affected forms through the authorized service provider or directly to the Corporate Registry; no new filing fee is charged if the requisition is cured within the prescribed correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles with the Alberta Corporate Registry and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; online via registered service provider or paper filing to the Corporate Registry counter in Edmonton, Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors with the Corporate Registry, and pay the statutory incorporation fee. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns the Alberta corporate certificate number. Keep the certified certificate for subsequent bank, tax and licensing filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses to issue the certificate because of a defect, file corrected Articles of Incorporation or a supplementary filing within the statutory cure period; in the case of an invalid incorporation, apply through the Court of King's Bench for relief or file Articles of Correction under s. 217 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Organizational Resolutions and Issue Initial Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate internal governance; no government filing required for the board resolution itself
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of directors or pass a unanimous written board resolution. Under the pro-forma first board resolution, accept the share subscription, issue the common shares, designate the registered office and registered agent, appoint officers, authorize banking arrangements, and approve corporate minute book records. Record all resolutions and share allotments in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreements or subscription records
Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or third party challenges corporate authority, issue a certificate of incumbency signed by the corporate secretary and provide the full board resolution, including officer appointment and share issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta provincial tax accounts activated through CRA Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Incorporation and Alberta corporate registry number to complete a CRA Business Registration Online request. Obtain the federal Business Number (BN), corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and any Alberta provincial corporate tax or employer health tax accounts applicable to the FPV drone manufacturing and retail operation.
required_dossiers: Principal place of business and registered office address
Bank account details or expected transaction information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the application because a BN already exists or information is incomplete, use CRA My Business Account to update program accounts or call CRA Business Enquiries to consolidate duplicate accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Annual Returns and Maintain Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain registered office and director records, notify the Corporate Registry of any change of registered office or directors within the statutory deadline, and file the annual return with the Alberta Corporate Registry by the anniversary date. Keep minutes, share registry, financial records and annual returns in the registered office for inspection.
required_dossiers: Notice of Change of Registered Office (if applicable)
Notice of Change of Directors (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is late or rejected, pay the prescribed late fee and refile; if the corporation is dissolved for non-compliance, apply for restoration under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) within the applicable reinstatement period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal business licensing authority of the local city/county in Alberta, together with Alberta Municipal Affairs – Safety Codes Branch for building and occupancy approvals
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence and Certificate of Occupancy for Manufacturing and Assembly Operation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act for the proposed small-scale carbon-fiber milling and brushless motor assembly; site-specific environmental registration or approvals may be required if wastewater discharge, air emission or hazardous waste thresholds are triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance required with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives, Alberta's Wastewater and Waste Control Regulations, municipal sewer discharge bylaws, and municipal air emission limits for volatile organic compounds from resin curing and solvent use; hazardous wastes such as resins, catalysts, carbon dust and lithium-ion batteries must be disposed through authorized waste carriers under Alberta hazardous waste manifest rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection approved by the local municipal fire department under the Alberta Fire Code; building permit and Certificate of Occupancy issued through the Safety Codes Act permitting process; workplace clearance from Alberta Occupational Health and Safety covering machine guarding, respirable dust control, noise exposure and lithium battery safety for the FPV drone assembly operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; CRA My Business Account portal and GST/HST NETFILE; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of Alberta Treasury Board and Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Alberta ULC incorporated in Canada obtains its statutory tax identifier by registering with the CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 (Request to Open a Business Number Program Account). A separate GST/HST program account (RT) is registered under the same BN. Non-resident entities carrying on taxable commercial activity in Canada must apply through the same RC1 process, provide corporate existence/officer information and a Canadian contact or authorized representative, and may be required to post security under the Excise Tax Act. No separate Alberta TIN exists; CRA BN is the single taxpayer identifier for federal and Alberta corporate tax and GST/HST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation in Canada; the Alberta ULC is a corporation for Income Tax Act purposes, files a T2 corporate return and is not fiscally transparent in Canada. Pass_Through_Eligible only for foreign (e.g., U.S. IRS check-the-box) classification on Form 8832, not for Canadian domestic tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box or fiscal-transparency election for an Alberta ULC. A U.S. investor may make an IRS check-the-box election to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. tax purposes, but Canada continues to tax it at entity level; hybrid mismatch and treaty-shopping rules (Income Tax Act s.18.4/18.6, General Anti-Avoidance Rule, and Canada-U.S. treaty limitation-on-benefits) may disallow deductions or deny treaty relief on hybrid structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST); Alberta applies federal GST only at 5% - no Alberta provincial sales tax or HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold based on total worldwide taxable supplies over the preceding four calendar quarters; a person ceases to be a small supplier once CAD 30,000 is exceeded in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, at which point mandatory GST/HST registration applies. Non-residents carrying on commercial activity in Canada are subject to deemed registration rules and must register if taxable supplies exceed threshold or if they request registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping. Registrants must issue invoices containing prescribed CRA particulars (supplier name, BN, invoice date, description, GST/HST paid/payable and rate) and retain copies; electronic invoices (PDF/XML/EDI) are accepted. GST/HST returns are filed electronically through CRA portals, and CRA uses risk-based audit and data matching rather than pre-clearance stamps for compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of FPV racing drones and related tangible components are zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act at 0% GST/HST when the goods are sold for export, shipped directly to a destination outside Canada (by the supplier, purchaser or common carrier), exported in commercial quantities, and supported by satisfactory contemporaneous export evidence. Supplies of ancillary digital services/software to non-residents outside Canada may also qualify for zero-rating. Domestic Canadian supplies remain subject to 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13A or authorized e-declaration record)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing movement of goods to the export destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign-exchange credit evidencing receipt and repatriation of export sale proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA data cross-checks export documentation; if contemporaneous proof is insufficient or the supply was not actually exported, the zero-rating is reversed and 5% GST/HST is assessed. CRA may deny zero-rating where foreign sale proceeds are not received or repatriated within 180 days. The normal reassessment period is four years, extended without limitation in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. Penalties include gross negligence penalties under section 285(1) of the Excise Tax Act of up to 50% of the net tax avoided, failure-to-remit penalties, interest, criminal prosecution for tax evasion, and, for a ULC, unlimited shareholder liability for unpaid corporate and GST/HST liabilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a convertible currency regime under the Bank of Canada Act. Capital account transactions are generally convertible for legitimate corporate purposes with no prior approval required for routine remittances. Current account transactions, including trade settlements, are fully convertible. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal, limited to standard tax filings and beneficial ownership disclosure; no significant regulatory barriers for routine FX flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Canada. Repatriation of export receipts is permitted without conversion. All exports must be reported to Statistics Canada within 90 days of shipment for balance of payments purposes. No statutory conversion ratios or timelines apply; transactions occur at market rates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for PayPal and Stripe as cross-border EMIs. Legal constraints include FINTRAC registration, AML/KYC compliance, and PCI-DSS adherence for international retail sales.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and video interviews permitted for corporate accounts; physical presence not required for standard onboarding but may be mandated for high-value transactions or complex cases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership discrepancies or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Articles of incorporation, director profiles, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and source of funds evidence

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits or adverse media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party sanctions reports, legal opinions, and business registration documents

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose code 'EQ' for equity or 'LOAN' for debt. Requires shareholder resolution, audited financial statements, and tax clearance certificates for verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements via SWIFT MT103 or commercial letters of credit. Requires invoices, shipping documents, and export compliance proof.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of incorporation; due no later than the last day of the month following the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late filing penalty; continued non-filing for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution after Director's notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year-end corporation, June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, minimum CAD 100; willful failure is subject to criminal penalties under the Income Tax Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue or asset threshold; independent audit is optional for a private Alberta ULC unless ordered by shareholder resolution or applicable under reporting issuer rules
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); financial statements are prepared annually to support the T2 filing and corporate records

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta Business Corporations Act does not impose a standalone annual UBO return for provincial ULCs; the annual return confirms registered office and directors, and beneficial ownership changes from share transfers are recorded in the register of members. Federal CBCA UBO register rules do not apply to this Alberta provincial entity

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 10,000 per engagement if an audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (Federal 15% + Alberta 8% general corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: combined federal and Alberta rate of 11% on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income; refundable SR&ED investment tax credit up to 35% for CCPCs and 15% for other corporations; Alberta innovation and manufacturing incentives may further reduce effective cash tax cost.
